title: CLR/151/2016 of Smt Gangesh Kumari Vs Kewal Sanon AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No.151 of 2016
Smt Gangesh Kumari Ö. Revisionist

Versus
Kewal Sanon & Others .Ö Respondents
Mr. Neeraj Garg, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. Piyush Garg, Advocate for the respondents.
2nd December, 2016
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
Having heard the rival contentions of both the
learned counsels, it transpires that the theme of the original
suit initiated way back 25 years ago was to declare the
execution of the sale deed null, void and illegal which was
executed by Raja Raghvendra Singh on dated 24.07.1965 and
registered on 04.08.1965. Shri Raja Raghvendra Singh so
executed the deed for himself and on behalf of his consort
Rani Sumitra Raje, who purportedly executed a power of
attorney dated 20.12.1962 for the purpose. The purchaser was
plaintiff Shri Kewal Sanon. After passing away of vendor Raja
Raghvendra Singh, the suit was filed by Shri Kewal Sanon,
seeking perpetual injunction restraining the defendants Smt.
Rani Sumitra Raje and Smt. Gangesh Kumari (daughter of
Raja Raghvendra Singh) from interfering in his possession.
 A joint counter claim was put up before the Trial
Court along with joint written statement. Against the interim
decision on the injunction application dated 24.02.1993
whereby the counter claim was also returned, two separate
revisions were filed in the Allahabad High Court, whereupon
the proceedings were stayed.
It transpires that somehow, the original suit was
dismissed by the Trial Judge at Dehradun Court on
15.02.2006, notwithstanding the stay granted by Allahabad
High Court was operating. After carving out of the state of the
Uttarakhand, the file stood transferred to this High Court and

2
after hearing the miscellaneous appeal, the counter claim was
restored on 04.05.2010. Original suit was also restored on
13.03.2012. Issues were framed on 05.07.2012 and
18.12.2012.
The learned Trial Judge decided issue no.2 and 4 on
05.02.2016, which pertained to the suit valuation and
payment of court fees payable by the plaintiff as well as by the
defendants on the counter claims.
The defendants feeling dissatisfied with such finding
of the learned Trial Judge moved a review application and the
order was modified on 11.05.2016, wherein it was held that for
cancellation of the sale ad valorem court fees has to be paid on
the market value of the property in question worth
Rs.1,86,01,525/- and the defendants were asked to pay the
court fees on such valuation.
I feel that cleverly defendant no.1 dropped herself
from the litigation and projected on surface only her daughter
defendant no.2 who moved the Amendment Application 728
(ka) pursuant to the order dated 11.05.2016. She wanted to
pay the court fees only on half of her share in the whole
property, all the same the deed of sale had to be cancelled as a
whole. So, his amendment application was rejected for the
simple reason that it was not in compliance of the order dated
11.05.2016.
Against this order, a writ petition (M/S) Application
no.2390 of 2016 was filed. Soon after its filing and making the
submissions partly before the writ Court, it was withdrawn by
petitioner/defendant no.2 with liberty to file fresh amendment
application. Order was also got that earlier amendment
application dated on 01.07.2016 shall also be deemed to be
withdrawn.
At the strength of the Writ Courtís order dated
29.08.2016, fresh amendment application dated 09.09.2016
was moved, which has been rejected by the impugned order
dated 09.11.2016.

3
 The whole force put forth by the learned counsel for
the defendant no.2 is that she is not concerned with the share
of the defendant no.1 (her own real mother) and she can be
asked to pay the court fees only to the extent of half of her
share, notwithstanding the cancellation of the whole sale deed
is being sought.
I feel that both the defendant no.1 and 2 are hand
in gloves and just to evade the payment of court fees, the
defendant no.1 has gone behind the curtain projecting her
daughter defendant no.2 on the outward surface. The sale
deed cannot be declared void to the extent of only half of her
share. The counter claim for cancellation of the sale deed is to
be allowed as a whole or not at all.
In view of what has been set forth above, there is no
force in the civil revision. It is hereby dismissed.
Defendants are advised not to file such type of
frivolous revisions and drag the litigation repeatedly before the
High Court because already three decades are going to pass
and the proceedings before the Trial Court could not step
ahead for hearing and producing the evidence by both the
parties.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
A.kaur/Pooja
